[[Field hockey]] made its [[Field hockey at the 1908 Summer Olympics|debut]] at the [[Modern Olympic Games]] as a men's competition in the [[1908 Summer Olympics|1908 Games]] in [[London]]. It was removed from the Olympic schedule of the [[Summer Olympic Games]] for the [[1924 Summer Olympics|1924 Paris Games]] and was reintroduced in the [[1928 Summer Olympics|1928 Amsterdam Games]]. The Women's field hockey was [[Field hockey at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|introduced]] into the Olympic programme at the [[1980 Moscow Olympics]].

The [[International Hockey Federation]] (FIH) was founded in 1924 and governs the field hockey events. Until the [[1988 Summer Olympics]], the tournaments were invitational, but a qualification system was introduced since the [[Field Hockey at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992 Barcelona Olympics]]. The last edition at [[2024 Paris Olympics|Paris]] was the 25th occurrence of the [[Field hockey at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|men's event]] and 12th consecutive occurrence of [[Field hockey at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|women's event]] in the Olympics.

[[India men's national field hockey team|India]] is the most successful team in the men's Olympic competition, having won a record eight gold medals. [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] is the most successful team in the women's competition, winning a record five gold medals. India also holds the record for the most appearances in the men's event with 22, while Netherlands and Australia hold the same record for the women's event, with 11 appearances each.

[[Great Britain men's national field hockey team|Great Britain]] won the first two editions of the men's event in [[Field hockey at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]] and [[Field hockey at the 1920 Summer Olympics|1920]]. [[India men's national field hockey team|India]] won the gold medal in seven out of eight Olympics from [[Field hockey at the 1928 Summer Olympics|1928]] to [[Field hockey at the 1964 Summer Olympics|1964]], with [[Pakistan men's national field hockey team|Pakistan]] winning three gold and silver medals each between the 1956 and [[Field hockey at the 1984 Summer Olympics|1984 Games]]. The matches are played on [[artificial turf]] since [[1976 Summer Olympics|1976]]. Since the late 1980s, European nations have dominated the field hockey events with [[Germany men's national field hockey team|Germany]] and [[Netherlands men's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] having won three gold medals each in the men's event. In the women's event, [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] and [[Australia women's national field hockey team|Australia]] have been dominant, having won five and three gold medals respectively since its introduction in 1980.

== History ==
[[Field hockey]] was introduced at the [[Modern Olympic Games]] as a men's competition at the [[1908 Summer Olympics|1908 Games]] in [[London]]. [[Great Britain men's national field hockey team|Great Britain]] won the first two editions in [[Field hockey at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]] (as [[England men's national field hockey team|England]]) and [[Field hockey at the 1920 Summer Olympics|1920]].<ref name="NBC">{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/field-hockey-101-olympic-history-records-and-results|title=Field hockey Olympic records and results|work=[[NBC Olympics]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> It was removed from the Olympic schedule of the [[Summer Olympic Games]] for the [[1924 Summer Olympics|1924 Paris Games]] because of the lack of an international sporting structure. The [[International Hockey Federation]] (FIH) was founded in Paris that year as a response to the same.<ref>{{cite web |title=History {{!}} FIH |url=https://www.fih.hockey/about-fih/history |access-date=2 February 2024 |work=[[International Hockey Federation]] |archive-date=2 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240202110108/https://www.fih.hockey/about-fih/history |url-status=live }}</ref> Men's field hockey was added to the Olympics for the next Olympic Games in [[1928 Summer Olympics|1928 Games]] held at [[Amsterdam]].<ref name="NBC"/><ref name="Olympedia">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/HOC|title=Hockey at the Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 August 2024|archive-date=15 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221215190142/https://www.olympedia.org/sports/HOC|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936.jpg|thumb|[[India men's national field hockey team|Indian team]] that won the gold at the [[India at the 1936 Summer Olympics|1936 Berlin Olympics]]]]

Starting in [[Field hockey at the 1928 Summer Olympics|1928]], [[India men's national field hockey team|India]] won the gold medal in seven out of eight Olympics till [[Field hockey at the 1964 Summer Olympics|1964]] including six consecutive gold medals from the [[1928 Summer Olympics|1928 Olympics]] to [[Field hockey at the 1956 Summer Olympics|1956]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/india-hockey-team-won-first-olympic-games-gold-medal-1928-amsterdam|title=How Indian hockey cast a spell to win the 1928 Olympics gold|date=3 April 2021|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[Olympics.com]]|archive-date=21 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821103744/https://olympics.com/en/news/india-hockey-team-won-first-olympic-games-gold-medal-1928-amsterdam|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="India">{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/how-indian-hockey-team-olympic-games-gold-medals|title=Indian hockey men at the Olympics: A gold-laden history|date=20 March 2020|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[Olympics.com]]|archive-date=21 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821103758/https://olympics.com/en/news/how-indian-hockey-team-olympic-games-gold-medals|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Pakistan men's national field hockey team|Pakistan]] won its first gold medal in [[Field hockey at the 1960 Summer Olympics|1960]] and won three gold and silver medals each in a run lasting from 1956 to [[Field hockey at the 1984 Summer Olympics|1984]].<ref name="Pakistan">{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/how-many-pakistan-olympic-medals-won|title=How many Olympic medals have Pakistan won|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[Olympics.com]]|archive-date=3 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403121251/https://olympics.com/en/news/how-many-pakistan-olympic-medals-won|url-status=live}}</ref> [[West Germany men's national field hockey team|West Germany]] won the gold medal in the [[Field hockey at the 1972 Summer Olympics|1972 Munich Olympics]], for the first gold medal by a non-Asian country since 1928. Olympic field hockey games were first played on [[artificial turf]] at the [[1976 Summer Olympics|1976 Montreal Games]] and was won by [[New Zealand men's national field hockey team|New Zealand]].<ref name="NBC"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/sports/olympics/olympic-history-how-artificial-surfaces-altered-the-balance-of-power-in-world-hockey-article-12779064.html|title=Olympic history: How artificial surfaces altered the balance of power in world hockey|date=27 July 2024|access-date=1 August 2024|work=Money Control|archive-date=30 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730161200/https://www.moneycontrol.com/sports/olympics/olympic-history-how-artificial-surfaces-altered-the-balance-of-power-in-world-hockey-article-12779064.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The domination of both the Asian countries came to an end in the late 1980s with India winning its last gold medal in the competition in [[Field hockey at the 1980 Summer Olympics|1980]] and Pakistan in 1984.<ref name="India"/><ref name="Pakistan"/>

Though the International Federation of Women’s Hockey Associations (IFWHA) was founded way back in 1927, [[Field hockey at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|Women's field hockey]] made its debut at the [[Summer Olympics]] only at the [[1980 Moscow Olympics]] and was won by [[Zimbabwe women's national field hockey team|Zimbabwe]]. On 23 April 1983, women’s hockey programme was taken over by FIH and the IFWHA was dissolved.<ref name="Olympedia"/> Great Britain won its first gold medal in the [[Field hockey at the 1988 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|men's event]] since 1920 in the [[1988 Seoul Olympics]].<ref name="NBC"/> 

[[File:Netherlands_womens_hockey_celebrate_-_2012_Olympics.jpg|thumb|left|[[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands women's team]] after winning gold at the [[Field hockey at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2012 Olympics]]]]

Until the 1988 Olympics, the tournament was invitational but FIH introduced a qualification system starting from the [[Field Hockey at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992 Barcelona Olympics]]. Since the 1990s, European countries have been dominant in the men's sport with the only exceptions being the wins by [[Australia men's national field hockey team|Australia]] in [[Field hockey at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004]] and [[Argentina men's national field hockey team|Argentina]] in [[Field hockey at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016]]. Both [[Germany men's national field hockey team|Germany]] and [[Netherlands men's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] have won three gold medals each, with the only other European winner being [[Belgium men's national field hockey team|Belgium]] in [[Field hockey at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020]].<ref name="NBC"/> In the women's events, [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] and [[Australia women's national field hockey team|Australia]] have been dominant, having won five and three gold medals respectively since its introduction to the Olympic programme in [[1980 Summer Olympics|1980]]. The only other winners of the women's event were [[Spain women's national field hockey team|Spain]] in [[Field hockey at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|1992]], [[Germany women's national field hockey team|Germany]] in [[Field hockey at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2004]], and [[Great Britain women's national field hockey team|Great Britain]] in [[Field hockey at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2016]].<ref name="NBC"/> 

The last edition of both the [[Field hockey at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|men's]] and [[Field hockey at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|women's events]] were held as a part of the [[2024 Paris Olympics]] with Netherlands winning both the events.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/photos/netherlands-women-secure-olympic-gold|title=Netherlands women secure Olympic gold|date=9 August 2024|work=[[International Hockey Federation]]|access-date=10 August 2024|archive-date=26 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826055645/https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/photos/netherlands-women-secure-olympic-gold|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/photos/netherlands-mens-team-strikes-gold-at-the-olympics|title=Netherlands men's team strike Olympic gold|date=10 August 2024|work=[[International Hockey Federation]]|access-date=10 August 2024|archive-date=26 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826055644/https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/photos/netherlands-mens-team-strikes-gold-at-the-olympics|url-status=live}}</ref> India holds the record for the most appearances in the Olympic men's competitions (22) and [[Spain men's national field hockey team|Spain]] has appeared in the most Olympic men's competitions (19) without winning the men's gold medal with the best place finishes being the silver medal won in [[Field hockey at the 1980 Summer Olympics|1980]], [[Field hockey at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996]], and [[Field hockey at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008]].<ref name="India"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2008-08-19/spanish-on-course-to-realise-olympic-dream/482492|title=Spanish on course to realise Olympic dream|date=19 August 2008|access-date=1 June 2024|work=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|archive-date=26 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826051758/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2008-08-19/spanish-on-course-to-realise-olympic-dream/482492|url-status=live}}</ref> Australia and Netherlands hold the record for the most appearances in the Olympic women's competitions (11).<ref name="Olympedia"/> India leads the medal tally for the men's events with 13 medals including eight gold medals. Netherlands heads the women's events with 10 medals including five gold medals and also leads the overall medal tally with 20 medals (eight gold, six silver and six bronze).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://khelnow.com/olympic-sports/top-five-records-of-indian-mens-hockey-team|title=Indian field hockey records|work=Khel Now|access-date=14 August 2021|archive-date=14 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814144944/https://khelnow.com/olympic-sports/top-five-records-of-indian-mens-hockey-team}}</ref><ref name="Olympedia"/>

== Olympic records ==
[[File:Hockey Final—India v. Great Britain at the Empire Stadium, Wembley, Thursday, August 12th. India scoring her third goal.png|thumb|[[India men's national field hockey team|India]] against [[Great Britain men's national field hockey team|Great Britain]] in the final of the [[Field hockey at the 1948 Summer Olympics|1948 Olympics]]]]

=== Men ===
*Most appearances: {{flagicon|IND}} [[India men's national field hockey team|India]] (22)<ref name="India"/><ref name="FIH">{{cite web|url=https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/news/mens-hockey-at-the-olympic-games-a-statistical-rewind|title=Men’s Hockey at the Olympic Games: A statistical rewind|work=[[International Hockey Federation]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=14 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614012227/https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/news/mens-hockey-at-the-olympic-games-a-statistical-rewind|url-status=live}}</ref>
*Most consecutive appearances : {{flagicon|IND}} India (18, {{GamesName|SOG|1928}} – {{GamesName|SOG|2004}})<ref name="India"/><ref name="FIH"/>
*Most medals: {{flagicon|IND}} India (13)<ref name="India"/><ref name="FIH"/>
*Most titles: {{flagicon|IND}} India (8)<ref name="India"/><ref name="FIH"/>
*Longest winning streak: 30 matches {{flagicon|IND}} (India, {{GamesName|SOG|1928}} – {{GamesName|SOG|1960}})<ref name="India"/>
*Most goals scored in a single tournament : {{flagicon|IND}} India (43, {{GamesName|SOG|1980}})<ref name="India1">{{cite web|url=https://khelnow.com/olympic-sports/top-five-records-of-indian-mens-hockey-team|title=Indian field hockey records|access-date=14 August 2021|archive-date=14 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814144944/https://khelnow.com/olympic-sports/top-five-records-of-indian-mens-hockey-team|url-status=live|work=Khelnow}}</ref><ref name="FIH"/>
*Fewest goals conceded in a single tournament: {{flagicon|IND}} India (nil, {{GamesName|SOG|1928}}, {{GamesName|SOG|1956}})<ref name="India1"/><ref name="FIH"/>
*Biggest margin of victory: {{flagicon|IND}} India 24–1 [[United States men's national field hockey team|United States]] ({{GamesName|SOG|1932}})<ref name="India1"/>
*Biggest margin of victory at an Olympic final: {{flagicon|IND}} India 8–1 [[Germany men's national field hockey team|Germany]] ({{GamesName|SOG|1936}})<ref name="India1"/>
*Most appearances by a player: {{flagicon|NED}} [[Teun de Nooijer]] ([[Netherlands men's national field hockey team|Netherlands]]), {{flagicon|AUS}} [[Ric Charlesworth]] ([[Australia men's national field hockey team|Australia]]), {{flagicon|ESP}} [[David Alegre]] and [[Pol Amat]] ([[Spain men's national field hockey team|Spain]]) (5 appearances)<ref name="FIH"/>
*Most goals scored by a player in a match: {{flagicon|IND}} [[Roop Singh]] (India, 10 goals vs United States at {{GamesName|SOG|1932}})<ref name="India1"/>
*Most goals scored by a player in an Olympic final: {{flagicon|IND}} [[Balbir Singh Sr.]] (India, 5 goals vs Netherlands at {{GamesName|SOG|1952}})<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/most-goals-scored-by-an-individual-in-an-olympic-hockey-final-(male)|title=Most goals scored by an individual in an Olympic hockey final (male)|work=[[Guinness World Records]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=26 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826063927/https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/most-goals-scored-by-an-individual-in-an-olympic-hockey-final-(male)|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Women ===
*Most appearances: {{flagicon|AUS}} [[Australia women's national field hockey team|Australia]] and {{flagicon|NED}} [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] (11)<ref name="FIHW">{{cite web|url=https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/news/womens-hockey-at-the-olympic-games-a-statistical-rewind|title=Women’s Hockey at the Olympic Games: A statistical rewind|work=[[International Hockey Federation]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=26 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826064739/https://www.fih.hockey/events/the-olympic-games-paris-2024/news/womens-hockey-at-the-olympic-games-a-statistical-rewind|url-status=live}}</ref>
*Most consecutive appearances: {{flagicon|AUS}} Australia and {{flagicon|NED}} Netherlands (11, {{GamesName|SOG|1980}} – {{GamesName|SOG|2024}})<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most medals: {{flagicon|NED}} Netherlands (10)<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most titles: {{flagicon|NED}} Netherlands (5)<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most goals scored: {{flagicon|NED}} Netherlands (192)<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most goals scored in a single tournament: {{flagicon|NED}} Netherlands (29, {{GamesName|SOG|2020}})<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most appearances by a player: {{flagicon|GER}} [[Natascha Keller]] ([[Germany women's national field hockey team|Germany]], 5 appearances)<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most goals by a player: {{flagicon|NED}} [[Maartje Paumen]] (Netherlands, 19 goals)<ref name="FIHW"/>
*Most goals scored by a player in a single tournament: {{flagicon|NED}}  [[Maartje Paumen]] (Netherlands, 11 goals at {{GamesName|SOG|2008}})<ref name="FIHW"/>
